subject: 20260913-172146-sweep-deepgram-30
headline: The voice agent exhibits outstanding quality and latency stability under scaling load, though a severe latency tail spike on the final turn of the conversation warrants investigation.

insights.title: Severe Tail Latency Spike on the Final Turn
insights.finding: The final turn of the conversation (turn 5) experiences a severe tail latency spike. While the median wait is an acceptable 833.3 ms, the p95 wait balloons to 3168.6 ms.
insights.why_it_matters: This wide gap means that although typical callers experience a prompt wrap-up, a portion of callers encounter an uncomfortable and jarring delay of over 3168.6 ms right before the call ends.
insights.next_step: Audit the prompt execution and state-closing logic specifically for the final turn of the conversation.

insights.title: Tail Latency Surprisingly Improves Under Load
insights.finding: Tail latency is at its worst during the single-concurrency baseline step (p95 of 2348.8 ms) and steadily improves as load scales up to 40 concurrent calls, dropping to a p95 of 1228.1 ms.
insights.why_it_matters: This inverse trend demonstrates that load is not the driver of latency degradation. It strongly points to early startup inefficiencies, such as connection or model cold-starts, which resolve themselves once the system is warmed up.
insights.next_step: Introduce a warm-up phase of synthetic traffic before initiating actual load measurements.

insights.title: Baseline Fails Coval Latency Target While Load Steps Succeed
insights.finding: The baseline step fails to meet the Coval load-testing target of 2000 ms, registering a p95 response time of 2348.8 ms. Under a peak load of 40 concurrent calls, the agent's p95 response of 1228.1 ms successfully complies.
insights.why_it_matters: Callers in low-traffic periods are exposed to sluggish response tails that violate industry targets, even though the system proves highly capable of meeting these performance standards under load.
insights.next_step: Analyze trace logs from the baseline step to determine if cold database queries or API handshakes caused the early tail slowdown.

insights.title: Insufficient Judge Sample Size Limits Test Trust
insights.finding: Out of 210 total completed calls across the entire test run, the LLM judge evaluated only 20 calls.
insights.why_it_matters: Relying on a tiny subset of 20 calls to assert quality is highly fragile. It is impossible to confidently verify conversational quality or detect edge-case failures across all load levels with such a small sample.
insights.next_step: Configure the evaluation harness to run the judge on a larger, statistically significant portion of all calls in future sweeps.

insights.title: Excellent Quality and Transcription Resilience Under Load
insights.finding: Transcription accuracy and conversational flow remain highly stable across all steps, with the mean Word Error Rate staying virtually flat between 2.9% in baseline and 3.0% at 40 concurrent calls, alongside zero interruptions.
insights.why_it_matters: The system does not sacrifice quality or experience conversational degradation (such as misheard words or accidental talk-overs) as user concurrency increases.
insights.next_step: Maintain the current transcription provider configuration since its quality characteristics are highly resilient under load.

insights.title: Response Latency is Dominated by LLM Thinking
insights.finding: At peak concurrency (40 calls), the agent's typical wait time (p50 ttfa) of 870.5 ms is heavily dominated by the thinking phase (p50 think_speak of 557 ms), whereas network round trips (85 ms) and endpointing silence detection (304.4 ms) are highly optimized.
insights.why_it_matters: Because transport and endpointing are already fast, efforts to shave milliseconds off the response time must focus squarely on the reply generation phase.
insights.next_step: Investigate model quantization or caching strategies to accelerate the thinking and reply generation stage.
